_doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the independent code review, TEMPLATE-OWNED, SHIPPED to every install (2026-09-26 external audit N4 fix, WP-S10). This file now ships a PORTABLE default: `review.model` and `review.reasoning_effort` are both null — NO model or effort pin at all, so a fresh install's Codex CLI simply uses its own current default model and reasoning effort. WHY: the previous shipped version hard-pinned the MAINTAINER's own account-specific model (first gpt-5.6-sol, then gpt-6-astra after gpt-5.6-sol returned HTTP 400 on that ChatGPT account) into a file every user's install carries — an account-specific fix leaking into a product default, flipping twice purely because of ONE account's own model access. THE SPLIT: an account that needs a real pin (e.g. the maintainer's) puts it in the SEPARATE, NEVER-shipped `config/orchestration/codex-review.user.json` (same shape, only the fields being overridden) — gitignored, excluded from the template sync, so it is per-machine/per-account state, never product state. `.claude/forge-bin/forge-codexreview-config.cjs::effectiveConfig(root)` merges shipped + user (user wins field-by-field) and `buildCommand()` derives the actual CLI invocation from the EFFECTIVE model/effort — omitting `-m`/`-c model_reasoning_effort=...` entirely when they are unset, so an unpinned install genuinely runs on the CLI's own default instead of silently inheriting a stale pin. Every consumer (the codex-reviewer agent, the forge-code-review skill, forge-codexreview.test.cjs) reads the EFFECTIVE config through that module (or applies the identical shipped+user merge rule by hand) — never this raw file alone, and never a model name restated from memory. History for context, not current behavior: gpt-5.6-sol pinned 2026-08-04 at effort max, raised to xhigh 2026-08-09; replaced by gpt-6-astra at xhigh on 2026-09-24 after gpt-5.6-sol returned HTTP 400 on the maintainer's account; both pins now live ONLY in that account's own codex-review.user.json, not here.

review._pin_doc: model/reasoning_effort are the PORTABLE default: null means 'no pin — use the codex CLI's own current default', deliberately never a specific model id here. An account that wants a specific model/effort sets both fields in the separate config/orchestration/codex-review.user.json; it is merged on top of this file by forge-codexreview-config.cjs::effectiveConfig() (user wins per field). Never edit a model name into THIS file for one account's convenience again — that is exactly the account-state-leaking-into-product-state bug this version fixes.
review._min_cli_doc: 0.156.1 is a general CLI-compatibility floor (the newest version this config's flags — -m, -c model_reasoning_effort=, -s, --strict-config — were live-verified against, 2026-09-24), not tied to any specific model. History for context: gpt-6-astra at xhigh was verified live 2026-09-24 on codex-cli 0.156.1 (ChatGPT login): codex exec -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh -s read-only --strict-config answered XHIGH-OK, exit 0 (20,517 tokens). gpt-5.6-sol needed >= 0.146.0 and was refused with HTTP 400 on the maintainer's account on 2026-09-24 — an outdated CLI can look exactly like a missing/refused model, so check `codex --version` before concluding a pin is unreachable.
review.command_doc: The REAL command is derived, never hardcoded here — see forge-codexreview-config.cjs::buildCommand(effectiveConfig(root)). Portable default (model/effort unset): codex exec -s read-only "<review prompt>". When an account's codex-review.user.json pins both: codex exec -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=<effort> -s read-only "<review prompt>".
review.adversarial_command_doc: Same derivation via buildCommand(effective, {adversarial:true}) — the prompt is prefixed 'ADVERSARIAL CODE REVIEW. <focus>' instead of '<review prompt>'; the -m/-c flags follow the exact same effective-model/effort rule as command_doc above.
review.long_thinking: expressed as model_reasoning_effort=<effort> when an account pins one (the highest level the CLI accepts is xhigh; no separate 'thinking' flag exists in codex-cli 0.156.1) — omitted entirely on the portable default, since there is no effort to raise on an unpinned model.

naming._naming_doc: Plans used to name this work package 'ECC code-review', which described the FALLBACK as if it were the plan. The planned step is the Codex pass; ECC review is only what you fall back to, and it is labelled as such. Deliberately model-agnostic here (WP-S10, 2026-09-26): the shipped label never names a specific model — an account with a real pin in codex-review.user.json may append '(<model>, effort <effort>)' via forge-codexreview-config.cjs::modelLabel()/effortLabel() when writing its own plan/report text, but the SHIPPED default must read the same on every install.

fallback.label: FALLBACK (non-independent) review — Codex did not run because: <reason>
fallback._fallback_doc: Never planned up front and never silently substituted: if Codex did not run, the report says so with the reason. An ECC pass is a second opinion from the same family of models that wrote the code, so it is not the independent review the owner asked for.

honesty._doc: If the EFFECTIVE model (shipped default, or an account's own codex-review.user.json pin) is unavailable (400 / CLI too old / not authed) or simply unset (the portable default), report the ACTUAL model that ran (from the CLI's own output) or 'Codex default model' — never the name of a model that did not actually run. A review attributed to any pinned model name that ran on something else is a fabricated provenance.

operational_notes.effort_is_slow: A review at a high reasoning effort (max, and to a lesser degree xhigh) regularly runs LONGER THAN 10 MINUTES. Measured 2026-08-04: a 3-file review was still running at the 10-minute mark and had to be relaunched in the background. Always run it detached (background) and wait for completion — killing it mid-flight wastes the whole run.
operational_notes.exec_host_handshake_can_fail: Measured 2026-08-04: one effort=max run returned MODEL-USED plus "the read-only execution host repeatedly failed during handshake, even on a no-op" — i.e. Codex could not read any file and produced NO review. A follow-up run on the same flags at effort=low read the config fine and echoed back the pinned values, so this is intermittent, not a broken configuration. If a run reports a handshake failure, it produced no review: rerun it, and never present it as a completed review.
operational_notes.model_cannot_self_identify: Asked which model it is, Codex answers "GPT-5 (Codex; exact deployment ID is not exposed)". That is normal — a model cannot reliably self-report its deployment. The trustworthy evidence that the pin took effect is the CLI header line (model: gpt-6-astra) plus the fact that the flags were passed; do not treat the model's self-description as a contradiction.
operational_notes.verified: 2026-09-24: codex exec -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh -s read-only --strict-config --skip-git-repo-check "Reply with exactly the text XHIGH-OK" -> XHIGH-OK, exit 0, codex-cli 0.156.1, ChatGPT login (owner re-enabled Codex). History: End-to-end proof 2026-08-04 (effort max): codex exec -m gpt-5.6-sol ... read this file and echoed back review.model=gpt-5.6-sol and review.reasoning_effort=max. Effort-wissel 2026-08-09: `codex exec -m gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh -s read-only --strict-config` draaide live en antwoordde XHIGH-OK — --strict-config bewijst dat de waarde herkend wordt en niet stil wordt genegeerd.
